newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel awards two licences for international phone service.
newsitem.headline: Israel awards two licences for international phone service.

text.p: Israel's Communications Ministry on Wednesday awarded licences for international phone service to two groups that include Sprint, Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom, SBC Communications and STET.

One of the winning groups includes Italy's STET, with 26 percent. SBC Communications (formerly Southwestern Bell) has 10 percent; Aureq Group (a joint venture between SBC and the Israeli Kahan Group), 25 percent; Israel's Globescom, 22 percent; and Kahan, 16.5 percent.

The other winning group comprises Clalcom, a subsidiary of Clal Industries with 44 percent; Sprint Corp with 25 percent; Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom, each with 10.5 percent; and Israel's Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd, with 10 percent.
The winning groups will compete with Bezeq Israel Telecom, the state controlled phone company.
Six consortia made up of Israeli and multinational companies submitted bids in the tender. The other four groups were:

- Bellsouth Corp ; Brazil's Safra banking group; the IDB Holding Group through its subsidiaries Discount Investment Group and PEC Israel Economic Corp ; Canadian based carrier Teleglobe Inc and Israsat International Communications Ltd.
- Tadiran ; British Telecom ; MCI Communications ; Israel's Idan Software Industries and Darcom.
- Korea Telecom; Leumi and Co, a Bank Leumi subsidiary; U.S. based Frontier Corp and Israel's Kardan Investments.
- Poalim Infrastructure and Technology, a Poalim Investments unit; Eurocom of Israel and Bell Atlantic.
One third of Bezeq's revenue and nearly half of its profits are from its international services.
Ministry officials have predicted that prices of foreign calls will drop by as much as 60 percent once competition begins.
